A fresh check found these problems in this version. Fix each one, and keep everything that is right:
- Remember, other: The remember line says science 'is validated' by review and repetition. The card only says checking 'helps validate' knowledge and that even well-checked findings can change, so the remember line makes validation sound more final than the card does.

rejected.title: Peer review and publication
card: Scientists publish their methods and results in journals. Other people can then see exactly what was done and how the conclusions were reached.
Peer review
before a journal publishes a study, independent experts in the same field read it. They check whether the methods suit the question and whether the results support the conclusions.
Replication
after publication, other scientists repeat the investigation using the published methods. If they get similar results, confidence in the finding grows.
Checking before and after publication helps validate scientific knowledge. Even a well-checked finding can change if new evidence appears.
rejected.remember: Science is validated when other experts check it, first in review and then by repeating it.

a.q: Why do scientists publish the methods they used, as well as their results?
opts: So other scientists can check and repeat the work
So other scientists can claim the findings as their own
So the results do not need to be tested any further
So the journal can decide which topics get studied
a.why: Published methods let other experts judge whether the work was sound and repeat it to see if they get similar results. Publishing does not end testing: even well-checked findings can change when new evidence appears.
a.clue: Think about what another scientist needs in order to repeat a study.

b.q: Dr Lee in Perth publishes a study showing a new fertiliser makes tomato plants grow taller. Another team follows her published methods and gets similar results. Which step is this, and what does it do?
opts: Replication, which builds confidence in her finding
Peer review, which builds confidence in her finding
Replication, which means no more testing is needed
Peer review, which means no more testing is needed
b.why: Repeating a published study with similar results is replication, and it builds confidence in the finding. Peer review is the check by experts before publication, so it is a different step. No check ends testing, because new evidence can still change a finding.
b.clue: Did the second team check the work before or after it was published?

b.q: Dr Lee in Perth finds that a new fertiliser makes tomato plants grow taller. Another team follows her published methods and gets similar results. What does this show?
opts: Her finding is more likely to be reliable
Her finding has now been peer reviewed
Her finding is proven to be true forever
Her finding must apply to every type of plant
b.why: Repeating a study with similar results builds confidence in the finding. This is replication, which happens after publication. Peer review is the check by experts before publication, so it is a different step.
b.clue: Did the second team check the work before or after it was published?

a.best: So other scientists can check and repeat the work

b.best: Her finding is more likely to be reliable
